place: flood and storm events in the US
source: Hong Kong and China. Numbers in the event text are from memory unless the note says checked.

event: Hurricane Katrina: the costliest US disaster in NOAA's billion-dollar series
Hurricane Sandy: record water level at the Battery (about 14 ft above MLLW)
Hong Kong Observatory's highest temperature on record: 36.6 °C
Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria: 2017 the costliest year in Swiss Re and NOAA records
Super Typhoon Mangkhut: No. 10 signal and a storm surge of about 2.35 m at Quarry Bay
Zhengzhou, Henan: 201.9 mm of rain in one hour; the State Council inquiry counted 398 dead or missing
Remnants of Ida: 3.15 inches of rain in an hour in Central Park
First reading above 40 °C in the UK: 40.3 °C at Coningsby, Lincolnshire; Heathrow 40.2 °C
Yangtze basin heatwave and drought: the longest and most intense on China's record
Black rainstorm: 158.1 mm in an hour at the Observatory, the most since records began in 1884
2024 the first calendar year more than 1.5 °C above pre-industrial (Copernicus ERA5: 1.60 °C)
Los Angeles wildfires: among the costliest insured wildfire losses on record (about $40bn)
